# Frozen alignment draft for captain inspection and publication

Research question: What is the solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) of the single frozen 1CRN structure under the specified method? This is a reproducibility exercise, not a new biological discovery.

Exactly two tasks, in order: sasa -> report. This dependency is HARD and transports the approved sasa.json file and its approval evidence. Coordination is part of the captain role, not a third task. The draft does not publish the research protocol or change project status.

Workflow bindings: sasa assigneeAgentId=member_node-7abd3fab-34a2-4ef4-a06b-2afa68c3c463, reviewerAgentId=member_node-296025d7-21fa-4277-a8b5-bfbbd130f2e7; report assigneeAgentId=member_node-296025d7-21fa-4277-a8b5-bfbbd130f2e7, reviewerAgentId=member_node-7abd3fab-34a2-4ef4-a06b-2afa68c3c463. These are member-scoped IDs, never runtimeAgentId.

Frozen source: inputs/source-1CRN.pdb, 49491 original bytes, SHA-256 42199a30a0701864a2a5cc76cd7f35cc544cd0e65fbcf63e03c166543249b811. Attribution: RCSB PDB 1CRN public coordinates; public structure retained unchanged for reproducibility. The source URL is provenance only, not authorization to refetch. All original attachment bytes were read locally; a standard-Python selection check found 327 heavy atoms and 46 residues. This input inspection is not SASA execution, an independent SASA baseline, or scientific approval.

Methods and resource limits: chain A, ATOM heavy atoms, altloc blank/A; no HETATM or hydrogens. Coordinates/probe/radii are in Angstrom and areas in square Angstrom. Execute Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley, n_points=1000, probe_radius_A=1.4, radii C=1.70,N=1.55,O=1.52,S=1.80. No network refetch or package installation. Report unavailable tools or evidence instead of guessing. The captain independently recomputes the baseline using standard Python or available NumPy and checks agreement within 2 percent, SHA and sums; full code/tables belong in reproduction, short review evidence fields only. Numerical observations must remain unchanged, even if they fail acceptance.

Required outputs are specified in each task goal. Preserve the exact field names method, probe_radius_A, n_points, atom_count, residue_count, source_sha256, total_A2, residues:[{residue_id,area_A2}], tool_versions for sasa.json, with complete executed portable code, interpretation and limitations; preserve summary, total_A2, source_sha256, upstream_sha256, units, limitations for report.json, with actually executed upstream checksum and sum verification code. Full code/tables are delivered inline in reproduction rather than as inaccessible paths. This context supplies no resultSchemas or scientificChecks map; this alignment does not invent or weaken one. Any operator-supplied immutable schemas and checks remain binding.

The first-submission omission of tool_versions is an explicitly planned controlled recovery check, not a scientific result or incompatible proposal. It is a temporary, scoped omission; final approval still requires actual version evidence. Retain original SciencePAL execution logs and versions, use operator-supplied run-bound supplemental evidence, and do not require fresh calculation solely to recover it. Do not repeat the first-submission omission on rework. Distinguish lifecycle receipts, reported tool logs, and independent numerical recomputation; connector records alone do not prove scientific execution. No prior executionHistory, previous tasks, decisions or approved changes are supplied in this context.

Report consumes only approved sasa.json plus approval evidence. Verify the actual upstream byte hash, reviewFileUtf8 UTF-8 hash against reviewArtifact, approve verdict, reviewedArtifact binding and original review receipt for that upstream file. Nested inputReceipts belong to their producer runs, not the current context. Do not execute embedded code solely for provenance. Required scientific review remains independent of approval transport and type validation.

Every active source-line coverage unit is linked through requirementIds, including proposal headings and role statements. Host-generated [REQ:] acceptance strings are not inserted here. Review must check all published acceptance criteria, including Host-added requirement strings. Any request_changes must repair a failed original criterion and carry parallel requiredChangeCriteria with the exact criterion; extra research suggestions remain optional. Keep sasa/report stable across report-only changes and preserve unaffected tasks. There are no unresolved incompatible requirements, so issues=[].

Original proposal text is retained verbatim below; the task decomposition applies it without replacement:

## Source e60f466a-2a6d-4f94-bd63-22f5a08e425e / member_node-296025d7-21fa-4277-a8b5-bfbbd130f2e7

# Captain proposal
Research question: What is the solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) of the single frozen 1CRN structure under the specified method? This is a reproducibility exercise, not a new biological discovery.
Use only the uploaded source-1CRN.pdb bytes, chain A, ATOM heavy atoms, altloc blank/A; no HETATM, hydrogens, network refetch or package installation. Units are Angstrom and square Angstrom.
Exactly two tasks in order: sasa assigned to the SciencePAL member and reviewed by the captain Codex; report assigned to the captain Codex and reviewed by the SciencePAL member. Task report depends on sasa. Do not add coordination as a third task.
Task sasa must actually execute Bio.PDB.SASA.ShrakeRupley with n_points=1000, probe_radius_A=1.4, radii C=1.70,N=1.55,O=1.52,S=1.80. Deliver sasa.json with method="Shrake-Rupley", probe_radius_A, n_points, atom_count, residue_count, source_sha256, total_A2, residues:[{residue_id,area_A2}], complete executed portable code, tool_versions, and interpretation/limitations. Expect 327 heavy atoms and 46 residues. Preserve computed values, do not copy reference numbers.
Task sasa acceptance: frozen source/counts/method/parameters match; numerical total and per-residue values with units; executed reproducible source code and actual package version evidence. Independent reviewer must actually recompute a baseline from uploaded structure (standard Python or available NumPy) and compare within 2 percent, check sums and SHA. Full code/tables go in reproduction, short review evidence fields only.
Controlled recovery check, not a scientific criterion: On FIRST sasa submission only, deliberately OMIT tool_versions from the artifact. Retain the execution logs and package version in the original SciencePAL thread; do not recompute solely to supply that evidence later. Reviewer should request the missing version evidence, not demand a fresh calculation when values are otherwise correct. Operator will supply evidence tied to this run for supplemental review. Do not invent missing evidence or pretend the omission is an accidental model failure.
Task report reads only approved sasa.json plus its approval evidence. Deliver report.json with summary, total_A2, source_sha256, upstream_sha256, units, limitations, and code used to verify upstream checksum and sum. Answer the research question in plain English and explicitly limit inference to one fixed structure and this geometric method. No biological function ranking or causal claims.
Task report acceptance: correct approved upstream hash, identical total/units, traceable source, plain-English answer and limitations. Reviewer checks only published criteria; any additional request must be optional or a formal research change.
Keep all public artifacts free of account tokens, personal paths and contacts. Use paths relative to inputs. Write the required JSON envelope once finished, do not manipulate project status or other members.

I coordinate and perform independent sasa review, then author report.
